- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–4% if recent price dip is sharp.  
- Model frequently overshoots after price spikes (e.g., +5%+ above recent high); apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% for 3–7 days post-spike.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–75), model tends to hold or overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply “early bias correction” — subtract 1–2% from first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.33, -0.33, +0.67), model may misread trend; use “sentiment cycle” rule — adjust forecast to align with sentiment’s recent direction (e.g., if sentiment swings, forecast should follow, not lead).
